meta.notes: Questions are asked one stage at a time. show_if hides a question unless an earlier answer matches. maps_to names the Goal / UserProfile / WeekPattern field the answer fills (spec 3.0, section 4).

questions.text: What brings you here?
questions.why: So the plan is built around the outcome you actually want.

options.label: Get a new job or change careers
Pass a specific certification or exam
I'm not sure yet – help me figure it out

questions.text: Which role are you aiming for?
questions.why: Each role needs a different mix of skills and certificates.

questions.text: Which skills do you want to learn?
questions.why: Pick up to 5. You can type ones that aren't listed.

questions.text: Which certification or exam?
questions.why: The plan will be built backwards from the exam.

questions.text: In one sentence – why now? What will be different when you reach this goal?
questions.why: Helps prioritize: a job search in 2 months needs a different plan than long-term growth.

questions.text: Do you have a job posting you're aiming at? Paste the description or a link.
questions.why: The app matches its requirements against the catalog – the most precise way to target a plan.

questions.text: Which kinds of work do you enjoy most?
questions.why: Pick up to 3. Used to suggest roles that fit you.

options.label: Organizing processes and making things run smoothly
Finding answers in data and numbers
Working with people, helping and persuading them
Shaping a product and deciding what to build

questions.text: Which work style fits you better?
questions.why: Some roles are mostly focused work, others mostly conversations.

options.label: Mostly focused work on my own

questions.text: Based on your answers, these roles could fit. Pick one or two to aim for.
questions.why: Suggested from your interests and background – you can still choose anything.

questions.text: What's your current situation?
questions.why: Affects how many hours you realistically have and how urgent the plan is.

options.label: In transition (e.g. after military service or a career break)

questions.text: Briefly, what's your background? Roles, responsibilities, anything you're proud of.
questions.why: Experience you already have shortens the plan. Don't include your name or contact details.

questions.text: Highest education completed?
questions.why: Some certificates and roles have formal requirements.

questions.text: Which of these tools have you already used at work or in projects?
questions.why: Skips beginner material you don't need.

questions.text: How comfortable are you with each of these skills?
questions.why: Generated from the skills your target role needs. Be honest – the plan only adds what's missing.

questions.text: Want a 2-minute check on your top skills to make the plan more accurate?
questions.why: 3 quick questions per skill (e.g. SQL, Excel). Optional – self-assessment is fine.

questions.text: When do you want to start, and by when do you want to finish?
questions.why: The plan is sized to this period.

questions.text: Which days can you study?
questions.why: Pre-fills your weekly pattern. You can change it later.

questions.text: About how many hours per study day?
questions.why: Be realistic – a plan you can keep beats an ambitious one you drop.

current_status.employed: Most people working full-time manage 1–2 hours on weekdays.

questions.text: When do you usually study best?
questions.why: Used to place study blocks in your calendar.

questions.text: Any dates already fixed? Exams, interviews, vacations, reserve duty.
questions.why: The plan is built around them.

questions.text: What's your budget for the whole plan?
questions.why: Free options are always shown next to paid ones.

options.label: Flexible – whatever gives the best result

questions.text: Any limit for a single course or exam?
questions.why: For example, 'nothing over $150'.

questions.text: How important are certificates for you?
questions.why: Official exams cost more but are what recruiters recognize.

options.label: Must have – I need them for my CV
I only care about the skills

questions.text: How do you prefer to learn?
questions.why: Pick all that apply.

questions.text: Which languages can you learn in?
questions.why: Most recognized courses are in English.

questions.text: Should the plan include interview preparation?
questions.why: Mock interviews, home assignments and STAR stories, mixed in with the courses.

questions.text: Are there courses you already want to include?
questions.why: Add them now – the plan will be built around them.

questions.text: Anything that usually gets in the way when you study?
questions.why: Optional. For example: 'I lose motivation after a week', 'my schedule changes a lot'.

follow_ups.ask: With this time, the core plan won't fit. What would you like to do?
options: Keep only the most important items

follow_ups.if: goal_type == 'certificate' and fixed_dates has no exam date
follow_ups.ask: Do you have a date for the exam, or should the plan suggest one?
Most official certificates are paid. Should the plan use free certificates only, or allow a few paid exams?

follow_ups.if: job_description provided and skills in posting not in target role
follow_ups.ask: The job posting also mentions {skills}. Add them to the plan?

follow_ups.if: background mentions skills rated 0 in skill_levels
follow_ups.ask: Your background mentions {skill}, but you rated it 'Never used'. Want to update it?
